purpose: Teach: ナンバーワン/しかるに/彷徨/踏み入れ/かなう/変人/親分/両足

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが村のナンバーワンの大工だった
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he was the best carpenter in the village.
lines.style: Distant, warm memory surfacing. Slow, deliberate pace. Voice reaches back gently—not quite present. Pause before her name, like gathering the memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、しかるにと古語をよく仰ったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and you'd often quote the old sayings the way your grandfather did, wouldn't you, dear?
lines.style: Affectionate agreement, slightly mischievous. Warm lilt on 'dear'—teasing him gently for his sentimentality. Knowing tone of someone remembering alongside him.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが戦地を彷徨った話をされた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he told us he'd wandered through the war zones.
lines.style: Voice quieter now, more careful. Pace slows further—this is harder to hold. Slight catch before the difficult words. Respectful of the weight of what he's saying.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、寺に踏み入れる時は脱帽されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and whenever he stepped into a temple, he'd remove his hat with such respect, wouldn't he, dear?
lines.style: Soft confirmation, almost to herself. Gentle nostalgia—she's seeing him do it. The 'dear' comes with quiet affection, acknowledging his piety alongside hers.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが「夢がかなう日」と仰った
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he'd say, 'The day when dreams come true.'
lines.style: Voice lifts slightly—this was something he believed. Warmth breaks through the wistfulness. Quotes it almost exactly as he heard it, like he's carried it all these years.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、村で変人と呼ばれた事もあったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, though in the village some called him eccentric, didn't they, dear?
lines.style: Wry affection. A small laugh buried in it—she's defending him and teasing him at once. The 'dear' carries both fondness and 'you know he was odd, and we loved him for it.'

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが家族の親分でいらした
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he was the pillar of our family.
lines.style: Voice steadies—this is the heart of it. Quiet pride underneath. Not boasting, but stating something true that still matters. Slight weight on 'pillar.'

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、両足で大地を踏み締めて生きてこられたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, he walked through life with both feet planted firmly on the earth, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Finality, tenderness, and closure layered together. Voice softens at the end—she's summing him up, sealing the memory. The 'dear' is almost a prayer. Trailing gently into silence.
